items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Narrator
In nineteen twenty, a man in Boston promised you fifty percent profit in just forty-five days.
Narrator
His name was Charles Ponzi. His idea sounded clever: postal reply coupons.
Narrator
Buy them cheap in Europe, cash them in America for more. A real price gap. On paper.
Narrator
But you couldn't do it at scale. So he paid old investors with new investors' money.
Narrator
Thousands lined up. He took in roughly fifteen million dollars in about eight months.
Narrator
Then the Boston Post started digging. By August nineteen twenty, it was over.
Narrator
Investors lost about twenty million dollars. That's over two hundred million today. The Post won a Pulitzer.
Narrator
Ponzi went to prison, was deported to Italy, and died broke in Rio in nineteen forty-nine.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the early profits were real, because they were your money.
Narrator
So when returns are huge and nobody can explain how, walk away.
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
